exact_checked_claims.claim: The ellipticity-projected tensor converges in global L2; the density converges in global C2; covariance 2S/mu and drift divS/mu converge locally uniformly. All sample sizes use dyadic prefixes. Any positive deterministic ridge tending to zero suffices.
Known-domain signed boundary extension and convolution give the required C2 and C2,2 bias convergence and polynomial derivative bounds; positivity and exact mass preservation are unnecessary.

Conormal elliptic regularity gives smooth positive-time pair density. Markov endpoint conditioning controls overlapping pairs; logarithmic bandwidth and dyadic nets give simultaneous almost-sure derivative convergence.

Derivative-sensitive kernel convergence gives H-to-C2 smoothing convergence; continuous functions t_+^2 and t_+^2 log(t) yield stable normal equations despite negative modes, zero crossings, repetitions and small positive eigenvalues.

All positive population modes span full local gradient/Hessian jets by compactly supported cutoff functions and graph-norm spectral approximation; local limiting normal matrices are coercive for each fixed truth and compact.
Finite Gram formulas are basis invariant and Borel without inversion of a possibly singular feature Gram matrix; measurable eigenbasis selection is unnecessary.

key_boundaries: The model assumes stationarity, reversibility, exact positions, a known fixed lag, a known smooth domain, smooth coefficients and known positive bounds. Nonreversible dynamics, measurement noise, unknown geometry and weaker regularity are not covered.
Reflection is conormal and depends on the tensor. Ordinary normal reflection is not an interchangeable boundary condition for anisotropic diffusion.

The raw tensor and separately fitted divergence converge locally uniformly in the interior. The global tensor conclusion is L² convergence after ellipticity clipping, not uniform boundary convergence or convergence of tensor derivatives.

No convergence rate, finite-sample guarantee, class-uniform conditioning bound, efficient numerical scheme or general-domain implementation is supplied. The all-mode estimator is a mathematical construction involving known-domain integrals.

Fixed-lag identification, spectral fitting and eigenvalue-power weighting have established predecessors. The claimed addition is consistency of this specific fit in the stated general tensor model, rather than the first multidimensional diffusion estimator.

The supplement also discusses a different estimator obtained from classical variational regularization. That argument does not prove consistency of the main spectral fit, and internal AI audits or finite controls do not constitute human peer review or formal proof certification.
